source.original_title: 05/07/2026 - Robbie Slim & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session
source.display_title: 05/07/2026 - Robbie Slim & Harry Edmonds KFS- Kettlebell Body Game Plan Session — Closed

setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: I know you spoke with Kim. He kind of gave me a little bit of a head start

prospect.name: Robbie Slim
prospect.location: Southern California, near Los Angeles, USA
prospect.family_status: Has a girlfriend; children are grown and moved out, selling the family house to downsize
prospect.training_background: About two years of consistent barbell, dumbbell and machine weightlifting, four to five days a week. Self-taught via the influencer Greg Plitt's website; has never worked with a trainer. No kettlebell experience.
prospect.medical: Chronic problematic left knee; persistent left hip / lower back tightness; persistent neck tightness with reduced rotation; intermittent shoulder issue. No diagnoses disclosed and the rep explicitly framed it as a collection of minor issues rather than anything structural.

signals: Already training four to five days a week for two years and eating a clean, self-managed diet
Goal is cosmetic refinement and mobility, not rescue: 'I don't need to be the strongest guy out there, just fit'
No pushback on the value of $6,000 — the only blocker was liquidity pending a house sale
Counter-signal: at 55 with several chronic joint complaints and self-reported inconsistency, he sits close to the rebuilder boundary

goals.text: Look fit with visible muscle definition and be confident with his shirt off, without being large
Lose the midsection fat and love handles
Bulkier arms — biceps have never responded to his training
Better mobility — get rid of the tightness and be able to follow a basic stretch routine without everything feeling tight
Have the knee, hip, back and neck pains dissipate or go away
Transition fully from barbells and machines to kettlebells, which he believes is a better whole-body workout
Acquire the knowledge to know he is training correctly and heavily enough

pains.text: Problematic left knee, managed by dragging a weighted sled backwards on leg day
Left hip and lower back area always tight
Neck always tight, cannot turn as well as he used to
Never had a trainer — no external check on whether he is lifting correctly or heavily enough
Misses workouts some weeks when work gets too busy
Afraid of hurting himself with kettlebells after watching YouTube workouts
Core work twice a week is 'clearly not working out that great'
Arms have never grown no matter how much he lifts

objections.raw_quote: But when I looked, you know, on YouTube, the... Workouts that can be done. I thought that looks like I'm going to screw something up on me and I don't want to get hurt. So I just didn't.
objections.rep_response: Validated it, then told a cautionary story about another prospect who injured his shoulder attempting a 70lb kettlebell unsupervised, and later framed the first month as pure form and technique mastery before any weight is added.

objections.raw_quote: Here's the thing. I'm selling my house right now. I have three interested parties. So, with the proceeds from that, I can do it. That's all good. But I have to wait till that happens.
objections.rep_response: Isolated the objection ('money out of the equation, logistics out of the equation, this is something that you want to do?'), then improvised two new payment structures on the spot: a 3k/3k split, or a $1,200 monthly plan carrying a $200/month premium that is waived if the balance is settled early.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two structures improvised live after the cashflow objection. Option A: $3,000 down and $3,000 on completion of the house sale. Option B (accepted): $1,200 to start covering the first month, then $1,200 per month, with the rep stating the monthly route is priced above the $6,000 upfront figure ('it's 1,200 a month, so it goes, obviously goes up from'). If the house sells, the prospect can settle the remaining balance and the per-month premium is removed. No single total contract figure was ever stated for the monthly route.

evidence: Prospect verbally accepted the $1,200 start: 'Yeah, yeah, like 1,200 would be good.'
Rep confirmed the choice — 'Do you want to do that, the $1,200?' — answered 'Probably easiest.'
Onboarding call with Trevor scheduled for Tuesday at 4:15pm Pacific; contact details verified on the call
Payment collection began live: rep asked 'Visa, MasterCard, Amex?', prospect answered 'It would be Visa. I have to move funds over'
Counter-evidence: the recording ends the moment the rep says 'Let me just remove the recorder out of the meeting', so payment is never confirmed as captured on the transcript
Counter-evidence: only the first $1,200 was in play; the remaining balance is contingent on a house sale the prospect estimates is one to two months out
outcome.cash_collection_basis: first_instalment_only; remaining balance contingent on a pending house sale and no total contract value was stated on the call
outcome.next_step: Onboarding call with Trevor, Tuesday 4:15pm Pacific; programme built within 24-48 hours after that call.

notable.note: Price moved from $6,000 upfront to a $1,200/month improvised plan within roughly two minutes of the prospect mentioning a pending house sale, with no financial-picture questions asked. The rep disclosed that the monthly route costs more than $6,000 but never stated the resulting total, so the prospect agreed to an open-ended figure. Separately, the prospect is 55 with four chronic joint complaints and an explicit fear of injuring himself with kettlebells, and no clinician clearance was ever raised.

quality.notes: Labels invert constantly. Whole exchanges are attributed backwards — e.g. at 00:02:06 the rep's question 'Are you doing kettlebells or are you doing different stuff?' and the prospect's answer are merged under the prospect label; the same happens at 00:05:41, 00:09:47 and 00:22:52. Role was read from content throughout. The prospect's label is a username, 'roba156', not his name.
